Wary

/WAIR-ee/ — rhymes with hairy · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Wary describes being cautious and on guard because you suspect possible danger or trouble.

The hikers were wary of the narrow bridge and tested each plank before stepping.

Worked Example

After a series of thefts in the neighborhood, the homeowner became wary, installing a new security system and checking the locks multiple times each night.

Wary precisely captures being on guard because you suspect danger, which is more exact than simply saying 'careful' or 'concerned.'

How Wary Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

cautious

cautious: careful to avoid danger or mistakes

suspicious

suspicious: believing someone or something cannot be trusted

leery

leery: informally distrustful and slow to trust

Antonyms

trusting

trusting: readily believing others without suspicion or doubt

unguarded

unguarded: relaxed, not watching for any danger

How Strong Is It? — cautious → suspicious → defensive → wary

cautious vs. wary

cautious vs. wary: Cautious is weaker than wary: a cautious person simply takes care, while a wary person is actively on guard because they sense possible trouble.

suspicious vs. wary

suspicious vs. wary: Suspicious is a step below wary in alertness — a suspicious person doubts one particular thing, while a wary person keeps a constant, watchful guard against whatever danger might come.

defensive vs. wary

defensive vs. wary: Defensive comes close to wary but stops just short: a defensive person shields what they have when challenged, while a wary person is already alert and scanning for the threat before it even appears.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — ware

Root — ware: watchful, alert, on guard (Old English)

Suffix — -y

Suffix — -y: full of, characterized by (Old English)

Put it together

Put it together: Wary joins the Old English root ware, meaning 'watchful and alert,' with the suffix -y, 'full of' — literally 'full of watchfulness,' which is exactly what a wary person is: cautious and on guard against possible danger.

Use the root in a new word: beware

Use the root in a new word: beware: The trail sign warned hikers to beware of loose rocks, so the wary climbers kept checking the cliff above them — both words come from the same old root for 'watch out.'

Word Choice

neutral / formal

Wary is your word for someone actively on guard because they suspect real danger or trouble. Reach for it when the caution goes beyond simple prudence—when there's actual distrust or watchfulness. For everyday carefulness, 'careful' is simpler.
